nodes.label: POST /generate tile render endpoint
nodes.rationale: Picks a geometry path automatically by grayscale correlation (threshold 0.90) against the calibrated room so a caller never has to declare which camera model applies; room dimensions on the form cannot override a real measurement.

nodes.label: POST /segment object extraction endpoint
nodes.rationale: Returns two full-size transparent layers (all_objects, mirrors) rather than one PNG per object, so compositing back over a retiled room is a plain alpha blend with no placement maths. Needs no calibrated geometry, so it works where /generate cannot.

nodes.label: POST /floor-wall endpoint
nodes.rationale: Runs only the floor/wall stage on one uploaded image as the fast way to inspect a mask; overlays are opt-in debug output and the source image is never modified.

nodes.label: engine.py metric tile projection
nodes.rationale: Stages 08h1 and 08h2 re-expressed as one parameterised vectorised function: every pixel is back-projected through the fitted camera, intersected with Y=0 or a wall plane, and the metric hit point indexes a tile+grout pitch grid. Kept untouched by the estimated path so both paths run the identical projection.

nodes.label: The clean room (emptied room render)
nodes.rationale: Surfaces are detected on the emptied room rather than the photograph because a chair hides the floor it stands on and SegFormer cannot label what it cannot see; measured wall coverage rose 0.662 to 0.889 and floor 0.1058 to 0.1107 on a 1408x768 room. It is explicitly a plausible reconstruction, not a photograph of what was really there.

nodes.label: extraction/inpaint.py LaMa windowed fill
nodes.rationale: big-lama ONNX export takes a fixed 512x512 input, so holes are filled per context window capped at 640 px with every hole written by exactly one window; the fill is composited with the mask as a stencil so outside_changed is 0. The mask is grown 2-8 px first because the ring just outside an object still holds its edge colour and contact shadow, which would leave a silhouette.

nodes.label: precise.py propose-localise-matte extraction
nodes.rationale: Runs the stage-06 idea with the models that actually install on this machine (ONNX CPU, no torch): SegFormer proposals, SAM boundary, guided-filter edge. About 11 s per photo on an i5-10400, in a worker thread so it does not stall the event loop.

nodes.label: segmentation.py fast single-model path
nodes.rationale: SegFormer-B4 plus connected components, no SAM and no matting, about 3 seconds: /generate only needs to know which pixels to protect from tiling, a job a binary mask does fine.

nodes.label: live_scene.py estimated camera synthesis
nodes.rationale: Synthesises a level unrolled pinhole at 67 degrees HFOV, 1500 mm above the floor, pitch solved by bisection so the predicted floor/wall junction lands on the photo's own far floor edge (2nd percentile of floor rows). Entered room dimensions drive that solve and therefore set tile scale. Wall tiling is rejected here because no wall-plane geometry is estimated.

nodes.label: pipeline_assets.py committed stage 06F4 cut-outs
nodes.rationale: Follows the pipeline's frozen rule that final prop RGB must come from the stage01 master input, never from a generated image. Cut-outs are written once into backend/generated/ and reused.

nodes.label: floor_wall.py two-class surface detection
nodes.rationale: Answers exactly one question with two strictly binary files and no ceiling or background output, adding no new model or dependency by reusing surfaces.py's cached ONNX session. No erosion, blur, opening, polygon fitting or colour thresholding, and no assumption about where a surface sits in frame.

nodes.label: surfaces.py ADE20K semantic segmenter
nodes.rationale: Its detect() argmax over all 150 classes is right for rejecting detections but loses floor where the network splits confidence, so floor_wall.py reuses the session but not the argmax.

nodes.label: Group-then-compare over per-class argmax
nodes.rationale: Summing each surface's ADE20K classes first fixes the case where floor 0.31 + rug 0.22 loses to wall 0.34, and makes the two masks disjoint by construction instead of by subtraction. A surface is held against the strongest single rival rather than the sum of all 149 others, which is what makes complete floor true; a ceiling stays out of the wall mask because the ceiling class wins its own pixels and a pixel it wins is in neither mask.

nodes.label: Band-limited GrabCut boundary refinement
nodes.rationale: The class map decides what is floor and wall; this decides where the line runs. The guided-filter snap lands on the image edge pixel by pixel and comes out ragged, so each boundary is re-cut with GrabCut inside a 1.2%-of-long-edge band (4-24 px) with pixels beyond the band locked and the other surface's core locked out, so the boundary can move but the region cannot be redrawn or grow. Deterministic with a fixed seed; roughness 1.043 to 1.020 and edge strength 358 to 460 across 21 rooms.

nodes.label: layers.refine_mask union cleanup
nodes.rationale: Closing at radius 1, connected-component speck filtering and hole filling capped at 0.2% of canvas so the gap between chair legs stays open. No erosion and no opening anywhere, because the first pixels they take are leaf tips, lamp flex, chair legs and the thin inner edge of a mirror frame.

nodes.label: Union instances before matting
nodes.rationale: Matting each object separately and stacking leaves a seam wherever two objects touch - a pillow's edge against the bed gets feathered as if the bed were background. One union and one matte makes such an internal boundary not an edge at all.

nodes.label: matting.refine and matting.decontaminate
nodes.rationale: A binary mask cannot be composited: it staircases on diagonals and carries a one-pixel rim of old background that reads as an outline. refine redraws the boundary as soft alpha following the photo's colour edges, moving it at most 2 px; decontaminate inpaints every partially transparent pixel from the object's own interior so what blends is the object's colour, not the room it was cut from.

nodes.label: SegFormer-B4 ADE20K proposals as SAM prompts
nodes.rationale: Each component becomes up to 3 positive points at the distance transform's peaks plus up to 4 negative points on the surrounding ring belonging to another class; the negatives are what stop SAM swallowing the wall behind a picture. Instance granularity is therefore limited to what SegFormer proposed - two merged adjacent paintings stay one object.

nodes.label: SAM ViT-B boundary localisation
nodes.rationale: Returns three candidates (part, subpart, whole) and the one agreeing best with the proposal wins, with its own IoU estimate breaking ties. SAM is only asked to refine proposed regions, never to find ones nobody proposed.

nodes.label: Containment merge within a label
nodes.rationale: Instances overlapping by more than 60% of the smaller one collapse, so a window split by mullions into four windowpane components returns as one window; merging only within a label keeps a pillow on a bed as its own object.

nodes.label: Mirror reflection instance rejection
nodes.rationale: A mirror reflects the room and SegFormer will find furniture inside the reflection, so any non-mirror instance lying 70% or more inside a mirror is dropped and reported in detections with its percentage. Mirrors are kept as a strict subset of the objects layer, enforced in the bytes that reach the file.

nodes.label: Trim instances against eroded surface map
nodes.rationale: A point prompt on a kitchen cabinet can lead SAM out across the polished floor it stands on, and a patch of old floor inside an object mask would paint itself back over the new tiles, so every instance is trimmed against the eroded wall/floor/ceiling map before joining a layer.

nodes.label: Mask2Former backend unavailable
nodes.rationale: It was the first choice but PyTorch 2.2.2 is the last macOS x86_64 wheel, was built against NumPy 1.x and raises 'Numpy is not available' under NumPy 2.x, while opencv-python-headless 5.0 requires numpy>=2. Supporting it means downgrading NumPy and OpenCV under the whole extraction pipeline, so backend='mask2former' raises that explanation rather than silently substituting something else.

nodes.label: torch not installable on this machine
nodes.rationale: PyTorch stopped publishing macOS x86_64 wheels after 2.2 and 2.2 has no cp313 build, so every model runs as onnxruntime on CPU with weights downloaded once into backend/models/.

nodes.label: Two geometry paths (fitted vs estimated)
nodes.rationale: Only the calibrated room gets measured geometry because the pipeline's GPU stages (Qwen empty room, SAM2 masks, stage08g3 fit) need CUDA; everything else is a plausible reconstruction and the README states that limit plainly rather than hiding it.

nodes.label: fitted path - calibrated room camera
nodes.rationale: Uses the camera stage08g3 actually fitted and is verified byte-for-byte against the committed output, so form-entered room dimensions cannot override a measurement.

nodes.label: estimated path - synthesised camera
nodes.rationale: Assumes a level camera, rectilinear lens and a photographer at one end of the room; a tilted or wide-angle shot will skew. Renders at up to 1600 px on the long edge, about 4 s end to end.

nodes.label: Parity against committed pipeline output
nodes.rationale: Verified against 08h2_props_over_metric_floor for the locked spec (600x1200 mm, 5 mm grout, rotation 0, both surfaces): mean absolute difference 0.19/255, maximum 7/255 from nearest-neighbour rounding order, no pixel off by more than 8.

nodes.label: surface=wall tiles the skirting course only
nodes.rationale: Limited to about 180 mm, the extent of 08b2_wall_screeding_mask; full wall tiling would need a wall-plane mask that stage 08b2 does not produce, and wall/both are rejected outright on the estimated path.

nodes.label: Simulated progress in TileVisualizer.tsx
nodes.rationale: The frontend's five steps run on a fixed 700 ms timer and are not driven by the server - stated as a known limit rather than presented as real telemetry.

nodes.label: backend/jobs/<job_id> output layout
nodes.rationale: Each request writes original, tile, raw (exact texture, no relighting), lit (relit, no props), result and state.json so each stage is inspectable; nothing prunes them.
